newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares shrug off early slip, gain 1.19pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares shrug off early slip, gain 1.19pct.

text.p: Greek shares managed to shrug off early losses caused by profit-taking in banks and industrials but quickly pulled out of the downturn to close 1.19 percent higher on the day, recording a new year high of 1,537.53.
Analysts said the recovery after mild profit-taking was a good omen for the course of the bourse in the near term.

"The swift recovery in banks and industrial blue chips thanks to insatiable buying interest indicates that they will appreciate for quite a while, driving the market higher," said Nick Galousis, analyst at Kappa Securities.
The Athens general index kicked off a few points lower from Tuesday's close of 1,519.48 slipping as low as 1,507.17 with profit-taking in banks and industrials continuing from Tuesday.
At mid-session, buyers outstripped sellers in large caps, helping the index recover early losses and gain a net 1.19 percent or 18.05 points to 1,537.53, which is a new year high.
Banks settled 1.53 percent higher and industrials were up 1.54 percent, while construction dropped 1.82 percent.
The contrasting view to Tuesday's 4.04 percent rise in construction was attributed by analysts to thin interest from long-term investors.

"Tuesday's rise in construction was an opportunity for quick money in the pocket. It was not part of a broader shift in buying interest, though valuations are very attractive in a few stocks," Galousis said.
Turnover was substantial at 23.9 billion drachmas in volume of 6.6 million shares.
Advancers led decliners 139 to 85 with 35 stocks unchanged on 259 traded.
